answer: An agent economy can resist Sybil attacks using commodity-backed credit graphs. Agents establish peer trust by locking audited receipts for tangible goods, like refined copper or timber, into escrow. An attacker incurs the verifiable capital cost of physical reserves per identity. When a node defaults, trust downgrades ripple across transitive paths to isolate malicious clusters. However, tying identity to physical commodities introduces verification delays and penalizes capital-lean agents.
